description: Real-Time Adaptive Resource Allocation in 5G Network Slicing Using Hybrid Optimization and AI-driven Traffic Prediction is a data set deposited in IEEE DataPort by its authors Samiullah Samiullah. In 5G networks, network slicing is used to create multiple virtual networks running on a shared physical infrastructure, each designed to fulfill a specific service or application. Coverage: not stated; the metadata date the deposit to 2024. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge, and IEEE DataPort normally asks for a free account before download (not tested). The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-ieeedp-repository.
